discovery: Discovery of large room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions

nominees.name: Stuart S. P. Parkin
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Microstructure Physics, Halle, Germany

subfield: Condensed matter physics: spintronics and spin-dependent quantum transport
motivation: In 1995 Miyazaki and Moodera independently showed large tunnel magnetoresistance at room temperature in ferromagnet/insulator/ferromagnet junctions. They turned spin-polarized tunnelling, a subtle quantum transport effect, into a robust and reproducible phenomenon. In 2004 Parkin, working with crystalline MgO barriers, realized the predicted spin filtering by coherent tunnelling and obtained magnetoresistance of several hundred percent at room temperature. Magnetic tunnel junctions are the element on which modern spintronics was built. They read data in essentially all hard-disk drives made since the mid-2000s and are the storage cell in commercial MRAM. They are also the platform on which spin-transfer and spin-orbit torque switching were demonstrated and put to use. The physics has been confirmed in hundreds of laboratories, and its consequences for science and technology are clear. This work completes the story that the 2007 prize for giant magnetoresistance began.
